models.summary.boogu-image-edit-turbo: Edits a single picture by written instruction in four steps: adding, removing or replacing things, restyling and changing text.
models.summary.boogu-image-turbo: A 10B model distilled to four steps, for photorealistic 1024px images with text in English and Chinese.
models.summary.chroma1-hd: An 8.9B model rebuilt from FLUX.1 schnell, with a wide range of styles and real negative prompts. Made as a base for fine-tuning.
models.summary.chroma1-radiance: A Chroma that draws pixels directly instead of going through an image decoder, which keeps fine detail. Still in training; this is its v0.4 release.
models.summary.ernie-image: The full ERNIE-Image model: slower than Turbo, with stronger instruction following and text rendering for posters, comics and structured layouts.
models.summary.ernie-image-turbo: Images in eight steps that follow detailed instructions and render text well, suited to posters, comics and multi-panel layouts.
models.summary.flux-2-klein-4b: A small, step-distilled FLUX.2 that makes 1024px images in four steps and edits pictures from one or more references.
models.summary.flux-2-klein-base-4b: The undistilled FLUX.2 klein 4B: slower, with more varied results, and the one to pair with fine-tunes and LoRAs.
models.summary.flux-schnell: Detailed 1024px images in four steps, with strong prompt following.
models.summary.hidream-o1-image-dev: An 8B model that works on pixels directly, with no separate text encoder or decoder. Strong at long text and layouts, and slow on most cards.
models.summary.iris-3b: A 3B model that draws 1024px images directly in pixels, without an image decoder. Detailed portraits and photographs, at a hundred steps.
models.summary.llada-image-turbo: A 6B model that makes images and edits them by instruction in four steps. Its text encoder is large, about 10 to 18 GB.
models.summary.longcat-image: A 6B model for photorealistic images that writes the words you put in quotes, in English and Chinese.
models.summary.longcat-image-edit: Changes a picture from written instructions in English or Chinese, leaving the parts you did not mention as they were.
models.summary.longcat-image-edit-turbo: A distilled LongCat-Image-Edit that changes a picture from written instructions in eight steps.
models.summary.minit2i-b-16: A minimalist research model that makes square 512px images in pixels. Small enough for modest graphics cards.
models.summary.moss-image: A 5B model, fine-tuned for clean layouts and legible text. It reads plain prompts, tag lists and JSON layouts that place text and objects.
models.summary.ovis-image-7b: A 7B model made to write text inside pictures, such as posters, banners and logos, while staying small enough for one graphics card.
models.summary.pixart-sigma: A small transformer that makes 1024px images in twenty steps, following long prompts through its T5 text encoder.
models.summary.qwen-image: A large 20B model that follows long prompts closely and writes long passages of text in English and Chinese. It needs a lot of memory.
models.summary.qwen-image-edit-2511: Changes pictures from written instructions, keeping people and objects consistent, and can combine up to three pictures. It can also edit the text inside a picture.
models.summary.qwen2.5-vl-7b: A language model that looks at pictures, so the assistant on this computer can tell whether what it made matches what was asked. It runs on the processor, about half a minute per picture. Qwen-Image and LongCat-Image read prompts with the same file.
models.summary.qwen3-4b-instruct: A language model that puts prompts into English, for the models that read only English. It runs on the processor, in a few seconds per prompt, and is the same file Z-Image reads prompts with: with Z-Image installed, nothing more is downloaded.
models.summary.real-esrgan-x4plus: Makes a picture four times larger and sharper, keeping it as it is. Small and fast: a 1024px picture comes out at 4096px in seconds.
models.summary.sd-1.5: The small 512px model that started local image generation. It runs on weak graphics cards and even on the processor alone.
models.summary.sdxl-base: The 1024px general-purpose model with the largest ecosystem of fine-tunes and LoRAs.
models.summary.sdxl-turbo: A distilled SDXL that makes a 512px image in a single step. The quickest way to try ideas.
models.summary.wan-2.1-i2v-14b-480p: Animates a picture into a 480p clip that starts from it and follows the prompt.
models.summary.wan-2.1-t2v-1.3b: Short 480p clips from text. The small Wan model, made to run on consumer graphics cards.
models.summary.wan-2.1-t2v-14b: Clips from text with more detail and steadier motion than the small Wan 2.1, at the cost of speed and memory.
models.summary.wan-2.2-i2v-a14b: Brings a picture to life: the largest open Wan model, making a clip that starts from the given frame and follows the prompt.
models.summary.wan-2.2-t2v-a14b: The largest open Wan model for clips from text, with two experts, one for the overall layout and one for detail. Strong at cinematic lighting and complex motion, but slow on consumer cards.
models.summary.wan-2.2-ti2v-5b: 720p clips at 24 frames per second, from text or from a starting picture. The Wan 2.2 model sized for a single consumer graphics card.
models.summary.z-image: The undistilled base model behind Z-Image Turbo: slower, but more varied, and it follows negative prompts. A good base for fine-tunes and LoRAs.
models.summary.z-image-l2p: Z-Image Turbo moved to pixel space: it draws pixels directly, with no image decoder. A research model that comes close to the original's prompt following.
models.summary.z-image-turbo: Photorealistic images in eight steps, and legible text in English and Chinese.

settings.providersIntro: Keys are stored on this computer and sent only to the provider they belong to. They are never shown again after saving.
settings.providersServer: Only the server's owner can add or change keys.
settings.serverKeysIntro: The server's keys, used by everyone allowed to use paid models, within their monthly limit. They are stored encrypted and never shown again.
settings.title: Settings
settings.translateCloud: {provider}, with your key (a fraction of a cent per prompt)
settings.translationIntro: Some models (SDXL, FLUX.1, Chroma) read prompts well only in English. With the translator installed, a prompt in another language is put into English for them, here on your computer, and you see what was sent.
settings.yourKeysIntro: Your own keys for paid services, used before the server's. What they spend is billed to you and does not count toward your monthly limit. They are stored encrypted and never shown again.
setup.intro: This server has no accounts yet. Enter the setup code from the server's log and create the owner's account: the owner can then invite everyone else.
setup.title: Set up this server
signin.forgot: Forgot your password? Ask the server's owner to reset it.
signin.title: Sign in

tokens.claudeCodeConfig: Either way, Claude Code saves the token in its own settings file (~/.claude.json), readable by your user on that computer.
tokens.claudeCodeHistory: Or keep the token off the command line altogether: paste it when asked by the first line, then run the second:
tokens.claudeDesktop: Add this to claude_desktop_config.json (Settings > Developer > Edit Config). Claude Desktop starts Hatchlight's command line, which must be installed on that computer, and it connects here:
tokens.intro: Let an agent such as Claude make pictures and videos here, as you. Make a token for each agent and choose what it may do: it can never do more than your account. Agents cannot install models.
tokens.name: Name
tokens.namePlaceholder: e.g. Claude Code on my laptop
tokens.once: Copy it now: it is shown only this once. Anyone who has it can act as you, within what it allows.
tokens.revokeQuestion: Revoke “{name}”? Agents using it stop working at once.
tokens.scopeGenerate: Make, upload and delete pictures and videos
tokens.scopeRead: See models, sessions and the gallery
tokens.stdio: For agents that start a command, with Hatchlight's command line installed. The token is passed in the environment, which, unlike an argument, other users of the computer cannot see in a process list:
training.askOwner: The server's owner can install the trainer.
training.captionPlaceholder: What it shows, e.g. a fox figurine on a table
training.consent: These pictures are mine to use, and every real person in them is an adult who agreed to this.
training.describeHint: A caption says what changes from picture to picture, such as the place, the pose and the light, and leaves the subject out: the trigger word learns the subject.
training.describeNeedsModel: Install Qwen2.5-VL in Models and the pictures can be described for you, in about half a minute each.
training.done: {name} is ready among your LoRAs. Write {trigger} in a prompt to call it up.
training.doneKept: {name} is ready among your LoRAs, kept at step {step}. Write {trigger} in a prompt to call it up.
training.install.checking: Checking the trainer can use the graphics card…
training.install.intro: Training runs on this computer and needs a trainer: Python, PyTorch and the training scripts. It downloads about {size} once, and needs an NVIDIA graphics card and Stable Diffusion XL.
training.install.packages: Installing PyTorch and what the trainer needs…
training.install.packagesHint: This is the large download. It shows no progress of its own and can take several minutes.
training.intro: Teach a model a subject or a style from your own pictures. You get a LoRA for Stable Diffusion XL.
training.name: Name
training.picturesHint: Use 10 to 30 sharp pictures of the subject or style, varied in angle and background. Only use pictures you have the right to, and never of a real person without their consent.
training.removeAsk: Delete the trainer and its downloads? Your LoRAs stay.
training.runningHint: Training uses the whole graphics card. Pictures you ask for wait until it ends.
training.samplesHint: Now and then it saves the LoRA and draws a sample with your trigger word. If a sample already looks right, stop there and keep it.
training.title: Train a LoRA
training.triggerHint: The trigger is a made-up word, such as qzporcelain, that goes before every caption. Put it in a prompt to call up what was learned. 800 steps take about 10 minutes on a 12 GB card.
ui.menuDescription: Sessions and the places of the app.
ui.toggleSidebar: Show or hide the side menu
update.body: It installs in a few seconds and Hatchlight opens again where you were.
update.failed: The update could not be installed. It will be offered again the next time Hatchlight starts.
users.disableQuestion: Disable {name}? They are signed out at once and cannot sign in until enabled again.
users.intro: Invite people with a link, and choose what each may do. Admins install models and manage people; only owners change the server's keys and settings.
users.inviteLink: Send this link to the person. It works once, for 7 days.
users.resetLink: Send this link to {name}: it lets them choose a new password, once, within 24 hours.
users.resetQuestion: Make a password link for {name}? Any earlier link stops working; their password stays the same until the link is used.
users.revokeInviteQuestion: Revoke this invite? Its link stops working.
users.title: People
welcome.lede: Each model draws in its own way. See the same prompt in each of them, check which runs best on your computer, and make your first picture.
welcome.prompt: Describe what you want to create
welcome.skip: Skip, I know my way around
welcome.suggestion.city: A rainy city street at night, neon reflections, cinematic wide shot
welcome.suggestion.fox: A red fox curled up in fresh snow, soft morning light, wildlife photo
welcome.suggestion.lighthouse: A lighthouse on a cliff at dusk, 35mm film, warm light in the windows
welcome.suggestion.ramen: A steaming bowl of ramen on a wooden counter, night market, shallow depth of field
welcome.title: Choose a model
